text: A wise prince ought to hold a third course by choosing the wise men in his state, and giving to them only the liberty of speaking the truth to him, and then only of those things of which he inquires, and of none others; but he ought to question them upon everything, and listen to their opinions, and afterwards form his own conclusions.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XXIII, How flatterers should be avoided
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
